questions.question:

He__ is living__ in this house for the past fifteen years before he shifted abroad.
questions.solution:
Here is the correct answer is **option 3) **

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/64e177b3c5c5cb81c12b3d5b5ddabaaf474cdad3d6098992ca6592786c8147d6.png] 

 In the above-given sentence, the error is in **option 3)**

__
 
• According to **The past perfect continuous tense **(also known as the past perfect progressive tense) shows that an action that started in the past continued up until another time in **the past. **
 
• The structure is given below:
 
 
• **subject + had been + Ving + object......+ since/for .**__
 
 

​

__
 
• **Since** is used for *point of time__* (1950, last month, etc.) whereas **for** is used *__for the duration__* ( 7 days, last year, etc). 
 
• In the given question"** had been living**" is used in place of "**is living**".
 
• As for the duration of time **"for"** is used in the given sentence.

 

 ** Hence the correct sentence is** - He __had been living__ in this house for the past fifteen years before he shifted abroad.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

__
 
• Use of **before** and **after** in a sentence 

 
 
• Both are used for two actions and when two actions take place one after another in the past ​ .
 
• The structures are given below:
 
 
• **Subject + had+ v3 +.........+ before + Subject + V2**__
 
• __**Subject + V2 + ...... + after + Subect + had + v3**__
 
 
 
 

 

__
 
• Use **"had+V3"** with the first action__ and **"V2**" with __the second action.__

 __
 
• Example- The doctor** had died*** before *__his wife **came.**
 
• **​**Example- She** told** me his name __*afte*r__ he **had** gone.

questions.question:
**Directions: Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank and make a grammatically correct sentence.**

The car park was full, so we ________ to look for another place to park.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **'had'**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• In the given blank, we need to use the past tense because the main clause has a paste tense of verb i.e. 'was full' the subordinate clause is formed by 'so'
 
• 'had' is the main verb of a clause and it is a past tense, not a past perfect tense if it was written like this 'had had' then it will be a past perfect tense because in this form 'had' is an auxiliary verb and 'had' is the main verb. 

**So the correct sentence is-** *The car park was full, so we **had** to look for another place to park.*

questions.question:
Identify the segment in the sentence which contains the grammatical error.

Each of these players have been warned not to repeat the silly mistakes.
questions.solution:
Here is the correct answer is **option 2) **

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/64e177b3c5c5cb81c12b3d5b5ddabaaf474cdad3d6098992ca6592786c8147d6.png] :-

​​​​​ In the above-given sentence, the error is in** option 2)**

__
 
• According to the **subject-verb agreement**, in a sentence, **the verb** must agree with **the subject**
 
• **"Each"** is an indefinite pronoun that does not agree with **'have'**.

 ** Rule**-* Either/neither/each/one **+of **+plural noun/plural pronoun **+ singular verb__***

__
 
• The phrase **' Each of **' takes a singular verb. So **"have"** would be replaced by **"has**".
 
• **Hence the correct sentence is** - Each of these players **has been** warned not to repeat the silly mistakes.**
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/87c1a28e731fadd9279228c1cea2f8e988a3f790bf9ccc89c9b0f02c423b1609.png] 
 
 
• **Indefinite pronoun**__- A **pronoun** that __does not refer to__ __a specific person__ or thing.
 
 

 **Examples**- Everyone,Noone,Someone ,Anyone,Each etc.

__
 
• **Definite pronoun **__ - A pronoun**** **that refers to a specific person or thing. Personal pronouns are also definite pronouns

 Examples- I, you, he, she, etc.

​ 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/51867102c7c2f369f6e29d2efe025e3b3367c68261ec20262828d84ca5c8f854.png] **__Hinglish__** 

__
 
• ** Subject verb agreement**** **के अनुसार, एक वाक्य में, **verb** (क्रिया ) को **Subject** से सहमत होना चाहिए I
 
• **Each** (प्रत्येक) एक अनिश्चित सर्वनाम है जो **have **से सहमत नहीं है।

 Rule-* Either/neither/each/one +of +plural noun/plural pronoun + singular verb__*

__
 
• वाक्यांश "**Each of** " एकवचन क्रिया लेता है। तो** have** को **has** से बदल दिया जाएगा।
 
• **अतः सही वाक्य है** -Each of these players has been warned not to repeat the silly mistakes.

 

​ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **अ****निश्चित सर्वनाम (Indefinite pronoun**__)- जिस सर्वनाम से किसी विशेष व्यक्ति या वस्तु का बोध न हो।

 **उदाहरण**- Everyone,Noone,Someone ,Anyone,Each आदि।

__
 
• **निश्चयवाचक सर्वनाम (Definite pronoun)__**__ __- जिस सर्वनाम से किसी विशेष व्यक्ति या वस्तु का बोध होता है। व्यक्तिगत सर्वनाम निश्चित सर्वनाम होते हैं l

questions.question:
Select the most appropriate option to substitute the underlined segment. If there is no need to substitute it, select No improvement

The child __smile on__ her mother
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **smiled at**. 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

Reading the sentence we find that:

__
 
• The incorrect preposition **on **is used along with the incorrect verb **smile**. 
 
• **On **is a preposition that is used to denote the position of something
 
• Therefore it cannot be used in this sentence 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__** 

The correct preposition here is **at**. 

 
• **At **is a preposition that **expresses the object of a look, thought, action or plan. **
 
• Here the object for the child's smile is the mother and the preposition **at **denotes that.
 
• **Example**: *I looked **at **my watch. *

*​*The correct verb here should be **smiled**.

 
• As per the context of the question, there are two possibilities. 
 
• The statement can be in the past tense or in the present tense. 
 
• Since the word **child **is **singular **it will be: The child smiles at her mother. 
 
• But this option is not given in the options. 
 
• Therefore we can go with the second option of the past tense. 
 
• I.e using the past tense verb **smiled**. 

The correct sentence will be: The child **smiled at **her mother.
